title.narrative: Scaling-up multi-sectoral assistance for people displaced multiples times and those recently affected by conflict and flooding for Northeast (Kachin)

description.narrative: ltpgtTwo years after the military takeover in Myanmar, the relentless violence continues, and we urgently need to step up our humanitarian efforts. With ongoing conflicts, a decline in public services, and rising inflation, communities are struggling more than ever, highlighting the pressing need to restore stability and security.ltbrgtWith 17.6 million people now in need of assistance, As violence spreads throughout the country, more individuals are exposed to daily threats and live in constant fear, emphasizing the urgent need for support.ltbrgtIn these challenging times, the vitality to save lives is greater than ever. As a frontline response organization, KBC is committed to delivering life-saving assistance to the targeted population and vulnerable individuals. The collaboration between KBC, MAG, and HI will enhance this response and support the capacity of local organizations , ensuring a more effective humanitarian effort. Humanity and Inclusion (HI) for technical support through programme and MAG will support the mainstreaming of EORE into KBC and consortium partners activities via the provision of EORE Training of Trainers to KBC. MAG will support organizations receiving ToT Mainstreaming to understand how to integrate EORE into their activities effectively and support the development of staff through ongoing online and in house training.ltbrgtIn this comprehensive project, we will address three key sectors to meet the needs of vulnerable populations including Vulnerable populations involving women, men, girls, boys, children, youth, elders, people with disability and the chronically illness. The food security focuses on providing essential food assistance to conflict-affected internally displaced people in Northeast Kachin, covering 1,589 affected IDPs in 1 camp. This will be carried out through cash transfers, ensuring access to basic food necessities over 2 months for Shwegu township ( 1 camp)period from February 2024 to February 2025 . Health services, a crucial component of this initiative, will be extended to 7 target areas spanning Shwegu, and Mansi townships. These regions have identified pressing health needs and gaps that require urgent attention. The project aims to provide comprehensive health support to a population of 8,100 comprising men, women, boys, and girls. To ensure the most effective and realistic services for these communities, regular guidance and consultation are sought from the Health Cluster and WHO. The range of services includes mobile clinics, community-based fixed clinics, patient referral support, and awareness-raising activities, and these sectors will be implemented by HMD.ltbrgtIn the humanitarian context, KBC is committed to providing support to Persons with Specific Needs (PSN) by addressing their unique challenges and vulnerabilities. Through the deployment of camp-based volunteers and existing church-formed committees, we aim to reduce the difficulties and concerns faced by both existing IDPs and those experiencing emergency situations. PSN and Protection assistance will cover 1050 displaced persons (273 Men, Women 337, 215 Boys and 225 Girls) during the project's duration, ensuring their safety, well-being, and dignity. KBC will provide Persons with Specific Needs (PSN) cash assistance to 140 population who are eligible with cluster criteria.ltbrgtlt/pgt
